definitions.explanation: A person who works under someone's supervision or command in an organization, workplace, or military.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}の{指導|しどう}も{管理職|かんりしょく}の{大切|たいせつ}な{仕事|しごと}だ。
examples.english: Training subordinates is also an important job for managers.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}との{信頼|しんらい}{関係|かんけい}を{築|きず}く。
examples.english: To build a relationship of trust with subordinates.

examples.japanese: {優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{部下|ぶか}に{恵|めぐ}まれている。
examples.english: I am blessed with excellent subordinates.

notes:
COMPOSITION: {部|ぶ} (section, division) + {下|か} (under). Literally "under the division/section."

CONTRAST:
・{部下|ぶか} ↔ {上司|じょうし} (subordinate ↔ boss/superior)
・Both are standard business vocabulary

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{部下|ぶか}を{持|も}つ (to have subordinates)
・{部下|ぶか}を{育|そだ}てる (to develop subordinates)
・{部下|ぶか}を{指導|しどう}する (to supervise subordinates)
・{部下|ぶか}に{任|まか}せる (to delegate to subordinates)
・{部下|ぶか}との{関係|かんけい} (relationship with subordinates)

RELATED TERMS:
・{上司|じょうし} (boss, superior)
・{同僚|どうりょう} (colleague)
・{後輩|こうはい} (junior colleague)
・{先輩|せんぱい} (senior colleague)
・チームメンバー (team member - more modern/neutral term)

USAGE NOTE:
{部下|ぶか} implies a clear hierarchical relationship. In modern Japanese business culture, some companies prefer flatter terms like チームメンバー or {担当者|たんとうしゃ} to promote a less hierarchical atmosphere.
